title: Kuching Half Marathon Heritage Run 2027 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: Kuching Half Marathon Heritage Run Review: Course, Heat, Cut-offs
meta_description: Kuching Half Marathon Heritage Run review: the AIMS-certified heritage route, 25°C and 94% humidity at the 4am start, a four-hour cut-off, 4,200 runners and the times it took to win.
dek: What Kuching's heritage half marathon was like in 2026: a pre-dawn run past the old town and the riverfront, still, saturated air, a generous cut-off and a field that mixes 82-year-olds with sub-1:17 racers.
verdict: Enter if you want a certified, chip-timed half marathon with a city break attached. The 2026 race drew 4,200 runners from 20 countries to AIMS-certified routes past Kuching's heritage buildings and riverside, with a 4am start, a four-hour cut-off and a finisher jersey on top of the medal. The catch is the air: at the start it was 25°C with 94% humidity and no wind, and it stayed that way to the cut-off, so it is not a course for a cool-weather personal best. The 2027 race moves from late July to Sunday 18 April.

sections.heading: The Course: Heritage Kuching Before Dawn
paragraphs: The race starts and finishes in central Kuching. In 2026 that was the boulevard of the MBKS (Kuching South City Council) building [1]; the 2027 race moves a short way to Dewan Masyarakat on Jalan Padungan [2]. The organiser bills the routes as a tour of the city's heritage: old buildings, riverside views and the murals promoted by the two city councils [1].

Both the 21.1 km and the 10 km routes are AIMS-certified [1], so the distance is right and a time here counts. With a 4am flag-off, a half marathoner runs most of the course in the dark; the 10 km starts at 6am, closer to first light [3].

sections.heading: The Weather: Warm, Saturated and Still
paragraphs: Kuching airport recorded 25°C at 4am on race morning, with a dew point of 24°C, 94% humidity and no wind [4]. Nothing changed for the next four hours: it was still 25°C at 7.30am, and at 8am, when the half marathon closed, humidity reached 100% [4]. Only after that did it warm up, to 28°C at 9am [4].

A dew point of 24°C to 25°C means sweat barely evaporates, and with no wind there is nothing to help it. Most of the field finished before the sun had any effect, so the race is warm rather than hot, but plan for a slower time than on a cool morning and drink early.
The 2027 race is in April rather than late July [2], so check the forecast in race week rather than relying on the 2026 readings.

sections.heading: Cut-offs and Finisher Items
paragraphs: The cut-offs are generous: four hours for the 21.1 km, two hours for the 10 km and one hour for the 5 km fun run [3]. Both competitive distances are chip-timed; the 5 km is not [3].

Every 21.1 km finisher inside the cut-off gets a medal and a finisher jersey, on top of the event jersey, and the first 100 finishers get a special top-100 jersey [3]. The 2026 medal design, called "Postage Stamp Legacy", drew on Kuching's heritage and wildlife, from the Irrawaddy dolphin to the stained glass of St Peter's Cathedral [1].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The race has separate open and national categories. Syahrullah Safri won the 21 km Men's National category in 2026 in 1:16:55, which was also good enough for third in Men Open; his twin brother Hazarullah, who had won the national category in 2024 and 2025, was second in 1:17:54 [5]. So in 2026 it took faster than 1:16:55 to win the open race, and a sub-1:18 to reach the national podium.

RM61,000 in prize money was spread across the competitive categories [1]. Most of the field runs for the experience, though: the oldest runner in 2026 was 82-year-old Lim Thiam Leng, who started racing at 71 and was back for a second year [5].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: In 2026, race packs were collected on the Friday and Saturday before the race, 11am to 6pm, at the Pullman Kuching [3]. For 2027 the collection dates and venue had not been announced when this was written, and registration closes on 8 March 2027 [2].

Seven in ten runners in 2026 were from Sarawak, but one in ten came from abroad [1]. The 2026 race was timed to coincide with the Kuching Food Festival [1]; with the 2027 race moving to April, that pairing may not repeat.

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a certified, chip-timed half marathon with a generous cut-off, a finisher jersey and a weekend in Kuching. It suits first-time half marathoners and runners who want a relaxed race abroad.
Think twice if you want a fast time in cool air: the 2026 race was run at close to 100% humidity with no breeze.

The 2027 race is on Sunday 18 April from Dewan Masyarakat, Jalan Padungan [2]. Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's race information, local reporting before and after the race, and airport weather records.

faqs.question: What changes at the Kuching Half Marathon Heritage Run in 2027?
faqs.answer: The date moves from late July to Sunday 18 April 2027, and the start moves from the MBKS Building boulevard to Dewan Masyarakat on Jalan Padungan. Flag-off times and cut-offs stay the same: 21.1 km at 4am with four hours, 10 km at 6am with two hours. Registration closes on 8 March 2027.

faqs.question: What is the cut-off for the Kuching Half Marathon Heritage Run?
faqs.answer: Four hours for the 21.1 km, two hours for the 10 km and one hour for the 5 km fun run. 21.1 km finishers inside the cut-off get a medal and a finisher jersey, and the first 100 get a special top-100 jersey.

faqs.question: How hot is the Kuching Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Warm and very humid rather than hot. At the 4am start in 2026 Kuching airport recorded 25°C, a 24°C dew point, 94% humidity and no wind, and it was still 25°C with 100% humidity at the 8am cut-off.

faqs.question: How fast do you need to be to win?
faqs.answer: In 2026 the 21 km Men's National category was won in 1:16:55, which was third in Men Open, and second national place took 1:17:54. There are separate open and national categories, with RM61,000 in prize money across the competitive races.

editorial_notes: Written 2026-10-26 about the previous edition (26 July 2026), on discovery of the 2027 race. Weather is from airport METAR observations (Kuching airport is about 10 km south of the start). Full results were not found, so only the national-category times reported by The Borneo Post are used; the Men Open winner's time is not known. Route maps were not available, so the course is described only as the organiser billed it. No rating: no participant reviews found.
